# Enterprise Software Coverage Matrix - 2026-05-21

This matrix reframes enterprise software coverage around one doctrine: oyatie is one unified ecosystem. The product goal is not to recreate per-department SaaS sprawl inside the repository. The product goal is to expose intuitive capability tiers on top of shared tenant, Cedar, ontology, workflow, audit, marketplace, identity, compliance, and observability primitives.

Per the 2026-05-21 clarification, the competitive thesis is: all consolidated into one ecosystem; one unified intuitive surface; no more per-department SaaS cycle. Vendor benchmark names still matter because buyers compare against SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, Salesforce, Workday, ServiceNow, Atlassian, Adobe, Okta, CrowdStrike, and similar incumbents. The implementation answer is capability-tier composition first, new flat microservice only when the benchmark proves a distinct operational concern.

Authoring guardrails: this document is a living coverage reference. It does not modify ADRs, standards, synthesis files, or microservice files. It points to the doctrines and marks gaps. The validator-owned implementation lanes decide when advisory rows become blocker rows.

## §1 Doctrine - Unified Ecosystem, Capability Tiers, and No SaaS-Sprawl Rebuild

| Doctrine | Mechanism | Matrix implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unified ecosystem | Every vendor benchmark maps into the same tenant, Cedar, ontology, workflow, audit-chain, compliance, and observability substrate. | Avoids a new island per department. |
| Capability-tier over microservice sprawl | ADR-0316 treats product surfaces as tenant activation bundles of permits, projections, workflows, UX shell manifests, compliance overlays, and telemetry. | Prevents CRM, marketing, learning, ITSM, and analytics from becoming duplicated identity/data/workflow stacks. |
| No-grouping flat catalog | ADR-0132 forbids suite or bundle microservices. Brand-layer grouping is allowed; architecture-layer bundling is not. | ERP platform, CRM platform, HR platform, and vertical platform folders are rejected. |
| Tenant as universal scope | ADR-0244 makes tenant plus sub-scope the routing, auth, retention, residency, audit, cost, and compliance primitive. | Every coverage row states tenant-scoped capability shape. |
| Substrate/product layering | ADR-0245 requires a tier field and cross-tier dependency discipline. | Shared services stay shared; products activate them without becoming gateways. |
| Marketplace settlement | ADR-0314 makes every tenant-to-tenant and tenant-to-consumer commercial exchange a DealSet. | Procurement, subscriptions, services, plugins, receivables, workforce contracts, and data licenses settle through one primitive. |
| Conglomerate hierarchy | ADR-0313 treats child tenants as sovereign tenants controlled through grants, not one giant parent account. | Enterprise benchmarks must work for subsidiaries, acquisitions, spinoffs, joint ventures, and regulated information barriers. |
| Dual personal/work boundary | ADR-0311 keeps personal tenant and employer tenant separate even when the same human uses both. | HR, learning, messaging, file, calendar, payroll, and marketplace rows preserve ownership boundaries. |
| Abuse-defense substrate | ADR-0297 sets anti-bot, anti-spoof, and anti-scrape controls across internet-facing surfaces. | Customer, marketplace, community, social, support, and public developer surfaces must inherit defense tiers. |
| Pack overlay verticals | Industry verticals are product/package overlays, not vertical-suite services. | Healthcare, finserv, insurance, public sector, education, manufacturing, and retail remain packs and projections. |

### §1.1 Capability-tier shape

1. Cedar permit set: every vendor row in §15 resolves to this shape or explicitly names why a new microservice is required.
2. Ontology projection: every vendor row in §15 resolves to this shape or explicitly names why a new microservice is required.
3. Workflow template: every vendor row in §15 resolves to this shape or explicitly names why a new microservice is required.
4. UX shell manifest: every vendor row in §15 resolves to this shape or explicitly names why a new microservice is required.
5. Compliance pack overlay: every vendor row in §15 resolves to this shape or explicitly names why a new microservice is required.
6. Observability and audit stream: every vendor row in §15 resolves to this shape or explicitly names why a new microservice is required.
7. Finops cost dimension: every vendor row in §15 resolves to this shape or explicitly names why a new microservice is required.
8. Migration/import declaration: every vendor row in §15 resolves to this shape or explicitly names why a new microservice is required.
9. Support runbook reference: every vendor row in §15 resolves to this shape or explicitly names why a new microservice is required.

### §1.2 New-microservice decision rule

A new microservice is allowed only when all four conditions hold:
1. The benchmark has a distinct operational bottleneck that cannot be owned by an existing service.
2. The benchmark needs distinct contracts, retention, SLOs, scaling, or failure modes.
3. The service can be single-concern and flat under ADR-0132.
4. The service has PR-143-grade documentation and validator coverage before production claims.

If those conditions do not hold, the benchmark becomes a capability tier over existing services.

## §2 Coverage Tier Model

| Tier | Definition | Required evidence | New service allowed? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Full existing coverage. Existing services already own the benchmark-class behavior at parity-or-better for common cases. | Service docs, permits, projections, workflows, and CI lanes already exist or are mapped. | No |
| B | Partial existing coverage. Existing services own the concern but still need depth or operating-bar completion. | Gap statement plus capability-tier backlog. | No by default |
| C | Composed coverage. Multiple existing services compose to cover the vendor surface. | Composition map plus Cedar, ontology, workflow, UX, compliance, and telemetry references. | No unless one subdomain proves distinct operational concern |
| D | New flat microservice required. No existing service owns the operational concern. | Named service, status, owner lane, PR-143 doc-set requirement, sequencing dependency. | Yes, flat single-concern only |
| E | Intentionally partner/plugin/out-of-core. | Plugin-app-store or marketplace partner path plus refusal boundary. | No core service |

### §2.1 Tier interpretation rules

1. Tier C is the preferred enterprise answer because it proves unified ecosystem behavior.
2. Tier D must name the exact new microservice and must not use suite names.
3. Tier A still requires CI evidence and operating-bar maintenance.
4. Tier B is not failure; it is a depth gap on an already-correct owner.
5. Tier E must be explicit so future agents do not accidentally scaffold low-priority partner surfaces.

ADR-0315 maps SAP-class ERP parity to flat service composition; ADR-0316 turns product names into capability tiers unless a distinct operational concern exists.

### §3.3 ERP operating-bar notes

#### §3.3.financial-accounting FI - Financial Accounting
- Coverage owner: payments + finops-portal + treasury + audit-chain; payments owns the first write boundary and every supporting service is an explicit handoff.
- Module data model: Financial Accounting normalizes general ledger document, company code, journal entry, open item, and tax line with source_system_ref, company_or_tenant scope, and audit_chain_ref preserved.
- Named UX surfaces: Manage Journal Entries, Display Line Items, and Trial Balance review; Oyatie maps them to shared task views instead of recreating an ERP module screen hierarchy.
- Integration and import: SAP/Oracle-style OData, BAPI/RFC, IDoc, SOAP, FBDI, CSV, and event extracts land in fixture erp-fi-01 with deterministic replay ids.
- Capability-tier status: C with treasury exists; the row stays a flat capability tier and does not authorize an erp-platform or module-bundle service.
- Cedar shape: payments.erp.fi.activate, payments.erp.fi.execute, audit.read.erp.fi; activation, execution, migration import, rollback, and audit read are separate default-deny actions.
- Ontology projection: ontology://erp/fi-financial-accounting@v1 with tenant, sub-scope, counterparty, region, pack, source-system, and audit-chain refs; objects carry tenant, sub-scope, counterparty, region, compliance pack, source id, and prior projection version.
- Workflow templates: workflow-template://erp-fi-activation-v1 and workflow-template://erp-fi-migration-evidence-v1; branches cover activation, migration evidence, exception approval, failed import quarantine, rollback, and sunset.
- Migration risk: general ledger document and company code can carry local customizing semantics, so imports must snapshot configuration and reject duplicate external ids.
- Market/moat note: ERP vendor lock-in here is module-specific process memory; Oyatie erodes it by moving general ledger document state into policy-backed workflow evidence.
- CI hooks: governance-erp-parity-module-map plus Cedar, ontology, workflow-template, and fixture-presence checks for erp-fi-01.

- Named UX surfaces: semantic-model editor, lineage graph, metric catalog, and dashboard review; Oyatie maps them to shared task views instead of recreating an ERP module screen hierarchy.
- Integration and import: SAP/Oracle-style OData, BAPI/RFC, IDoc, SOAP, FBDI, CSV, and event extracts land in fixture erp-data-23 with deterministic replay ids.
- Capability-tier status: C with data-warehouse in-flight for OLAP; the row stays a flat capability tier and does not authorize an erp-platform or module-bundle service.
- Cedar shape: analytics.erp.data.activate, analytics.erp.data.execute, audit.read.erp.data; activation, execution, migration import, rollback, and audit read are separate default-deny actions.
- Ontology projection: ontology://erp/data-data-and-analytics@v1 with tenant, sub-scope, counterparty, region, pack, source-system, and audit-chain refs; objects carry tenant, sub-scope, counterparty, region, compliance pack, source id, and prior projection version.
- Workflow templates: workflow-template://erp-data-activation-v1 and workflow-template://erp-data-migration-evidence-v1; branches cover activation, migration evidence, exception approval, failed import quarantine, rollback, and sunset.
- Migration risk: dataset and semantic model can carry local customizing semantics, so imports must snapshot configuration and reject duplicate external ids.
- Market/moat note: ERP vendor lock-in here is module-specific process memory; Oyatie erodes it by moving dataset state into policy-backed workflow evidence.
- CI hooks: governance-erp-parity-module-map plus Cedar, ontology, workflow-template, and fixture-presence checks for erp-data-23.

## §4 CRM + Customer-Engagement Stack

CRM is a capability tier over a shared customer/account graph. Sales, service, loyalty, marketing, and support do not create separate identity or audit islands.

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Forrester Wave CRM Software Q1 2025; Gartner customer engagement, CPQ, personalization, marketing categories.

### §4.2 Capability-tier details

#### §4.2.1 Salesforce Sales Cloud
- Vendor delta: Salesforce Sales Cloud is treated as a CRM + Customer-Engagement Stack benchmark, not as a suite clone; row id CTR-017 resolves to crm first and then to crm + ontology + workflow-engine + mail + calendar + analytics.
- Canonical objects: top objects are Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, and Forecast; the import contract records source_system_ref, source_object_ref, tenant_id, owner role, and audit_chain_ref for each object family.
- Operator screens: distinctive surfaces are Lightning Sales Console, Opportunity Workspace, Pipeline Inspection, and Forecasts; Oyatie keeps the task grammar in the shared shell while preserving these operator affordances as named workflow views.
- Connector shape: source integration uses REST, Bulk API, Metadata API, Pub/Sub or Streaming events, and AppExchange package metadata; adapters must expose deterministic pagination, idempotent replay keys, and export provenance.
- Subsuming service: crm subsumes the capability at C - composed capability-tier coverage; supporting services remain explicit handoffs instead of hidden bundle ownership: crm + ontology + workflow-engine + mail + calendar + analytics.
- Import route: bulk API export to JSON/CSV with replayed event deltas; reconcile Account identity merges, consent flags, and historical activity timelines; sample fixture cap-001-salesforce-sales-cloud includes 37 records, 11 relationship edges, and evidence hash sha256:salesforce-s.
- Cutover hazard: custom objects, managed packages, and automation side effects must be replayed around Account, not merely copied; rollback freezes new writes, replays deltas into a shadow projection, and restores the prior ontology pin without destructive deletion.
- Buyer profile: enterprise premium tier, complex procurement, administrator-heavy rollout, and high switching cost; the customer profile is represented by tenant scale, compliance pack, administrator count, and migration-window tolerance.
- Lock-in removed: metadata, AppExchange, admin certification, and pipeline history become portable capability-tier facts instead of platform captivity; the competitive claim is only valid when the user can leave the vendor-specific screen without losing Account history.
- Cedar guard: Cedar action family stays crm.capability.salesforce_sales_cloud.activate + crm.capability.salesforce_sales_cloud.execute + audit.read.salesforce_sales_cloud; default deny covers activation, execution, export, rollback, and audit read separately.
- Graph pin: ontology://salesforce_sales_cloud/TenantScopedProjection@v1 maps Account, Contact, and Lead into TenantScopedProjection nodes with retention_class and source_object_ref preserved.
- Process template: workflow-template://salesforce-sales-cloud-activation-v1 + workflow-template://salesforce-sales-cloud-evidence-review-v1 carries activation, migration import, evidence review, exception approval, rollback, and sunset branches with SLA timers.
- Validation hook: CI lane governance-coverage-matrix-salesforce-sales-cloud asserts data-model objects, named UX surfaces, connector type, migration fixture, market posture, and moat-erasure text are non-empty.
- Settlement / marketplace shape: commercial obligations settle as ADR-0314 DealSet entries; non-commercial Salesforce Sales Cloud events still emit audit evidence so free-tier or internal-use rows cannot bypass provenance.
- Observability values: metric capability_tier_activation_total{vendor="salesforce-sales-cloud",tier="C"}; trace span capability.salesforce-sales-cloud.activate; sample monthly volume 1,337 normalized events.
- Source boundary: factual product names come from the vendor/category surface already captured in this matrix plus the references in §19; architecture authority remains ADR-0132, ADR-0244, ADR-0314, and ADR-0316.

## §5 HR / Talent / Workforce Stack

Workforce product labels become program, talent, payroll, learning, and performance tiers over identity, community, workplace-integration, payments, workflow, and ontology.

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Forrester HCM Solutions Wave Q4 2025; Gartner HCM Suites for 1,000+ Employee Enterprises.

## §6 ITSM + IT-Operations Stack

IT operations is a workflow and ontology tier: tickets, incidents, assets, changes, CMDB, on-call, and evidence run on existing operational substrates unless paging or ITSM ownership requires an in-flight flat service.

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Gartner ITSM Platforms; Forrester collaborative work and security operations references.

### §6.1 Category coverage table

| Vendor benchmark | Surface | Representative capabilities | Oyatie composition | Status | Tier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ServiceNow ITSM | IT service management | incident, problem, change, request, service catalog, CMDB | itsm + workflow-engine + ontology + observability + audit-chain | in-flight service or capability tier required | D - new microservice required |
| Jira Service Management | ITSM and service desk | requests, incidents, assets, change, on-call adjacency | itsm + tasks + workflow-engine + community + observability | in-flight service or capability tier required | C - composed capability-tier coverage |

| PagerDuty | incident response | paging, escalation, service ownership, incident workflows | incident-management + observability + messenger + workflow-engine | in-flight service or capability tier required | D - new microservice required |

## §7 FP&A + Analytics + BI Stack

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Gartner Analytics and BI Platforms; Gartner Financial Close; Forrester BI and enterprise applications research.

## §8 Document + Content + Collaboration Stack

Collaboration surfaces are first-class product tiers over existing workspace services. CLM, whiteboard, and design-collaboration are distinct in-flight services only where data model and interaction shape justify them.

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Gartner content, document, intranet, CLM, and collaboration categories; Forrester CWM and DXP references.

### §8.1 Category coverage table

| Vendor benchmark | Surface | Representative capabilities | Oyatie composition | Status | Tier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Microsoft 365 | office collaboration | Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneDrive, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint | docs + sheets + slides + drive + mail + messenger + sites | covered by existing services | A - full existing coverage |
| Google Workspace | office collaboration | Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Gmail, Meet, Calendar, Forms, Sites | docs + sheets + slides + drive + mail + meet + calendar + forms + sites | covered by existing services | A - full existing coverage |
| Apple iWork | productivity platform | Pages, Numbers, Keynote, iCloud collaboration | docs + sheets + slides + drive | covered by existing services | A - full existing coverage |
| Box | enterprise content management | files, governance, classification, retention, workflows | drive + governance + compliance + workflow-engine | covered by existing services | A - full existing coverage |
| Dropbox | file collaboration | sync, share, signatures, replay, capture | drive + docs + recordings + workplace-integration | covered by existing services | A - full existing coverage |

### §8.2 Capability-tier details

#### §8.2.1 Microsoft 365
- Vendor delta: Microsoft 365 is treated as a Document + Content + Collaboration Stack benchmark, not as a suite clone; row id CTR-104 resolves to docs first and then to docs + sheets + slides + drive + mail + messenger + sites.
- Data model delta: top objects are Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneDrive, and Outlook; the import contract records source_system_ref, source_object_ref, tenant_id, owner role, and audit_chain_ref for each object family.
- UX delta: distinctive surfaces are Microsoft workspace, Microsoft file/document view, Microsoft approval or signature flow, and Microsoft sharing settings; Oyatie keeps the task grammar in the shared shell while preserving these operator affordances as named workflow views.
- Integration delta: source integration uses Microsoft Graph, Dataverse Web API, OData feeds, webhooks, and Power Platform solution exports; adapters must expose deterministic pagination, idempotent replay keys, and export provenance.
- Oyatie mapping: docs subsumes the capability at A - full existing coverage; supporting services remain explicit handoffs instead of hidden bundle ownership: docs + sheets + slides + drive + mail + messenger + sites.
- Migration extract: API and CSV export with incremental replay; map Word identifiers, attachment provenance, permissions, and workflow state before write cutover; sample fixture cap-088-microsoft-365 includes 37 records, 11 relationship edges, and evidence hash sha256:microsoft-36.
- Migration risk: field-level permissions, custom statuses, and historical attachments must survive normalization of Word; rollback freezes new writes, replays deltas into a shadow projection, and restores the prior ontology pin without destructive deletion.
- Market posture: midmarket-to-enterprise tier with domain-specialist buyer and material switching cost; the customer profile is represented by tenant scale, compliance pack, administrator count, and migration-window tolerance.
- Moat erosion: Microsoft 365 or Dataverse adjacency becomes a connector shape rather than a tenant-wide product gravity well; the competitive claim is only valid when the user can leave the vendor-specific screen without losing Word history.
- Policy/action proof: Cedar action family stays docs.capability.microsoft_365.activate + docs.capability.microsoft_365.execute + audit.read.microsoft_365; default deny covers activation, execution, export, rollback, and audit read separately.
- Ontology projection proof: ontology://microsoft_365/TenantScopedProjection@v1 maps Word, Excel, and PowerPoint into TenantScopedProjection nodes with retention_class and source_object_ref preserved.
- Workflow proof: workflow-template://microsoft-365-activation-v1 + workflow-template://microsoft-365-evidence-review-v1 carries activation, migration import, evidence review, exception approval, rollback, and sunset branches with SLA timers.
- Evidence lane: CI lane governance-coverage-matrix-microsoft-365 asserts data-model objects, named UX surfaces, connector type, migration fixture, market posture, and moat-erasure text are non-empty.
- Settlement / marketplace shape: commercial obligations settle as ADR-0314 DealSet entries; non-commercial Microsoft 365 events still emit audit evidence so free-tier or internal-use rows cannot bypass provenance.
- Observability values: metric capability_tier_activation_total{vendor="microsoft-365",tier="A"}; trace span capability.microsoft-365.activate; sample monthly volume 13,256 normalized events.
- Source boundary: factual product names come from the vendor/category surface already captured in this matrix plus the references in §19; architecture authority remains ADR-0132, ADR-0244, ADR-0314, and ADR-0316.

## §9 Identity + Governance Stack

Identity and governance are substrate tiers over tenant, Cedar, audit, compliance, and ops control surfaces. Product labels never bypass ADR-0244 tenant scope or ADR-0311 personal/work separation.

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Gartner identity verification, PAM, consent, GRC, and HCM categories; Forrester CIAM references.

## §10 Cybersecurity + Privacy Stack

Security product surfaces are defense tiers over edge, identity, policy, observability, audit-chain, compliance, and abuse-defence controls from ADR-0297.

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Forrester Security Analytics Platforms Q2 2025; Gartner PAM, observability, CNAPP, NDR, firewall, privacy categories.

## §11 Developer-Platform Stack

Developer platform capability tiers land on Foundry, developer-sdk, cloud-iac, workflow, observability, feature flags, and plugin-app-store rather than a new developer suite.

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Gartner cloud-native, API management, developer productivity, testing, observability categories; Forrester app-development services references.

## §12 Industry-Vertical Stack

Verticals are products and pack overlays, not new vertical-suite services. Industry specificity lives in Cedar fragments, ontology projections, compliance packs, workflow templates, and marketplace/plugin categories.

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Gartner industry cloud and vertical software categories; Forrester vertical application references.

## §13 Consumer + Personal-Use Surface Coverage

Consumer surfaces activate the same tenant, identity, Cedar, ontology, workflow, audit, and privacy substrate. Personal and work tenant boundaries from ADR-0311 decide ownership.

Benchmark reports / research anchors: Consumer benchmark surfaces used as product-parity references, not as enterprise-market drivers.

### §13.2 Capability-tier details

#### §13.2.1 WhatsApp
- Vendor delta: WhatsApp is treated as a Consumer + Personal-Use Surface Coverage benchmark, not as a suite clone; row id CTR-212 resolves to messenger first and then to messenger + meet + identity + api-gateway.
- Data model delta: top objects are Conversation, Contact, Message, Media Attachment, and Group; the import contract records source_system_ref, source_object_ref, tenant_id, owner role, and audit_chain_ref for each object family.
- UX delta: distinctive surfaces are WhatsApp mobile home, WhatsApp account/settings, WhatsApp sharing screen, and WhatsApp history/export; Oyatie keeps the task grammar in the shared shell while preserving these operator affordances as named workflow views.
- Integration delta: source integration uses OData services, IDoc/BAPI extraction, CDS views, and SAP Integration Suite events; adapters must expose deterministic pagination, idempotent replay keys, and export provenance.
- Oyatie mapping: messenger subsumes the capability at A - full existing coverage; supporting services remain explicit handoffs instead of hidden bundle ownership: messenger + meet + identity + api-gateway.
- Migration extract: phased extract using CSV/XML plus API deltas; preserve Conversation natural keys, fiscal calendars, and cross-module posting provenance; sample fixture cap-196-whatsapp includes 37 records, 11 relationship edges, and evidence hash sha256:whatsapp0000.
- Migration risk: customizing tables and extension fields can change Conversation semantics by company code, so imports must carry configuration snapshots; rollback freezes new writes, replays deltas into a shadow projection, and restores the prior ontology pin without destructive deletion.
- Market posture: enterprise premium tier, complex procurement, administrator-heavy rollout, and high switching cost; the customer profile is represented by tenant scale, compliance pack, administrator count, and migration-window tolerance.
- Moat erosion: module customization and consultant lock-in are narrowed to typed import fixtures and flat service owners; the competitive claim is only valid when the user can leave the vendor-specific screen without losing Conversation history.
- Policy/action proof: Cedar action family stays messenger.capability.whatsapp.activate + messenger.capability.whatsapp.execute + audit.read.whatsapp; default deny covers activation, execution, export, rollback, and audit read separately.
- Ontology projection proof: ontology://whatsapp/TenantScopedProjection@v1 maps Conversation, Contact, and Message into TenantScopedProjection nodes with retention_class and source_object_ref preserved.
- Workflow proof: workflow-template://whatsapp-activation-v1 + workflow-template://whatsapp-evidence-review-v1 carries activation, migration import, evidence review, exception approval, rollback, and sunset branches with SLA timers.
- Evidence lane: CI lane governance-coverage-matrix-whatsapp asserts data-model objects, named UX surfaces, connector type, migration fixture, market posture, and moat-erasure text are non-empty.
- Settlement / marketplace shape: commercial obligations settle as ADR-0314 DealSet entries; non-commercial WhatsApp events still emit audit evidence so free-tier or internal-use rows cannot bypass provenance.
- Observability values: metric capability_tier_activation_total{vendor="whatsapp",tier="A"}; trace span capability.whatsapp.activate; sample monthly volume 28,052 normalized events.

### §14.1 Center-of-gravity policy

1. High-count services require stronger review because one permit or ontology mistake affects many vendor benchmark tiers.
2. A center of gravity may not become a suite owner. It owns primitives; product tiers activate those primitives.
3. Every new benchmark row must be traced to at least one center and one bounded owner service.
4. The coverage-matrix CI lane should fail when a vendor row lacks Cedar, ontology, workflow, or CI references.

### §15.1 Registry cards

#### CTR-001 - SAP S/4HANA
- Registry delta: SAP S/4HANA is treated as a ERP Stack benchmark, not as a suite clone; row id CTR-001 resolves to payments first and then to payments + finops-portal + marketplace + workflow-engine + ontology + crm + production-planning + quality-management + plant-maintenance + supply-chain-planning + global-trade + warehouse + treasury + real-estate + compliance.
- Canonical objects: top objects are Company Code, Cost Center, Material, Sales Order, and Production Order; the import contract records source_system_ref, source_object_ref, tenant_id, owner role, and audit_chain_ref for each object family.
- Operator screens: distinctive surfaces are Fiori Launchpad, Manage Journal Entries, Manage Sales Orders, and Monitor Material Coverage; Oyatie keeps the task grammar in the shared shell while preserving these operator affordances as named workflow views.
- Connector shape: source integration uses OData services, IDoc/BAPI extraction, CDS views, and SAP Integration Suite events; adapters must expose deterministic pagination, idempotent replay keys, and export provenance.
- Subsuming service: payments subsumes the capability at C - composed capability-tier coverage; supporting services remain explicit handoffs instead of hidden bundle ownership: payments + finops-portal + marketplace + workflow-engine + ontology + crm + production-planning + quality-management + plant-maintenance + supply-chain-planning + global-trade + warehouse + treasury + real-estate + compliance.
- Import route: phased extract using CSV/XML plus API deltas; preserve Company Code natural keys, fiscal calendars, and cross-module posting provenance; sample fixture cap-001-sap-s-4hana includes 37 records, 11 relationship edges, and evidence hash sha256:sap-s-4hana0.
- Cutover hazard: customizing tables and extension fields can change Company Code semantics by company code, so imports must carry configuration snapshots; rollback freezes new writes, replays deltas into a shadow projection, and restores the prior ontology pin without destructive deletion.
- Buyer profile: enterprise premium tier, complex procurement, administrator-heavy rollout, and high switching cost; the customer profile is represented by tenant scale, compliance pack, administrator count, and migration-window tolerance.
- Lock-in removed: module customization and consultant lock-in are narrowed to typed import fixtures and flat service owners; the competitive claim is only valid when the user can leave the vendor-specific screen without losing Company Code history.
- Cedar guard: Cedar action family stays payments.capability.sap_s_4hana.activate + payments.capability.sap_s_4hana.execute + audit.read.sap_s_4hana; default deny covers activation, execution, export, rollback, and audit read separately.
- Graph pin: ontology://sap_s_4hana/TenantScopedProjection@v1 with source_system_ref, source_object_ref, normalized_object_type, retention_class, and audit_chain_ref maps Company Code, Cost Center, and Material into TenantScopedProjection nodes with retention_class and source_object_ref preserved.
- Process template: workflow-template://sap-s-4hana-activation-v1 + workflow-template://sap-s-4hana-evidence-review-v1 with activation, evidence review, migration import, rollback, and sunset branches carries activation, migration import, evidence review, exception approval, rollback, and sunset branches with SLA timers.
- Validation hook: CI lane governance-coverage-matrix-sap-s-4hana asserts data-model objects, named UX surfaces, connector type, migration fixture, market posture, and moat-erasure text are non-empty.
- Settlement / marketplace shape: commercial obligations settle as ADR-0314 DealSet entries; non-commercial SAP S/4HANA events still emit audit evidence so free-tier or internal-use rows cannot bypass provenance.
- Observability values: metric capability_tier_activation_total{vendor="sap-s-4hana",tier="C"}; trace span capability.sap-s-4hana.activate; sample monthly volume 1,337 normalized events.
- Source boundary: factual product names come from the vendor/category surface already captured in this matrix plus the references in §19; architecture authority remains ADR-0132, ADR-0244, ADR-0314, and ADR-0316.

#### CTR-002 - Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP
- Registry delta: Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP is treated as a ERP Stack benchmark, not as a suite clone; row id CTR-002 resolves to payments first and then to payments + finops-portal + marketplace + workflow-engine + ontology + compliance + treasury + supply-chain-planning + warehouse.
- Record family: top objects are Ledger, Project, Supplier, Purchase Order, and Journal Batch; the import contract records source_system_ref, source_object_ref, tenant_id, owner role, and audit_chain_ref for each object family.
- Daily workflow: distinctive surfaces are Navigator, Smart View, Scheduled Processes, and Transaction Console; Oyatie keeps the task grammar in the shared shell while preserving these operator affordances as named workflow views.
- API seam: source integration uses Oracle REST resources, SOAP services, FBDI/ADFdi bulk loads, and BI Publisher extracts; adapters must expose deterministic pagination, idempotent replay keys, and export provenance.
- Capability tier: payments subsumes the capability at C - composed capability-tier coverage; supporting services remain explicit handoffs instead of hidden bundle ownership: payments + finops-portal + marketplace + workflow-engine + ontology + compliance + treasury + supply-chain-planning + warehouse.
- Migration payload: phased extract using CSV/XML plus API deltas; preserve Ledger natural keys, fiscal calendars, and cross-module posting provenance; sample fixture cap-002-oracle-fusion-cloud-er includes 37 records, 11 relationship edges, and evidence hash sha256:oracle-fusio.
- Normalization issue: field-level permissions, custom statuses, and historical attachments must survive normalization of Ledger; rollback freezes new writes, replays deltas into a shadow projection, and restores the prior ontology pin without destructive deletion.
- Commercial segment: enterprise premium tier, complex procurement, administrator-heavy rollout, and high switching cost; the customer profile is represented by tenant scale, compliance pack, administrator count, and migration-window tolerance.
- Competitive wedge: platform lock-in around canonical records, consultant customization, and cross-module process memory; the competitive claim is only valid when the user can leave the vendor-specific screen without losing Ledger history.
- Permit scope: Cedar action family stays payments.capability.oracle_fusion_cloud_erp.activate + payments.capability.oracle_fusion_cloud_erp.execute + audit.read.oracle_fusion_cloud_erp; default deny covers activation, execution, export, rollback, and audit read separately.

## §16 Aggregate Gap Count - New Microservices Needed

The live repository contains 56 top-level microservice directories after the ERP scaffolds. The 9 ERP scaffolds already exist in the working tree: production-planning, quality-management, plant-maintenance, crm, supply-chain-planning, global-trade, warehouse, treasury, and real-estate. The B2B-leader expansion remains in-flight and sets the target at 69+ microservices, not at another suite.

| Gap bucket | Named surfaces | Count | Status | Claim boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ERP scaffolds already present | production-planning, quality-management, plant-maintenance, crm, supply-chain-planning, global-trade, warehouse, treasury, real-estate | 9 | existing-scaffold | Operating bar and PR-143 artifact sets still required; do not count as future unknowns. |
| B2B-leader core in-flight | marketing-automation, contact-center, performance-management, learning-management, itsm, incident-management, financial-planning, data-warehouse, contract-lifecycle-management, whiteboard, design-collaboration, data-pipeline, healthcare-integration | 13 | in-flight | Minimum path from 56 to 69. |
| B2B-leader plus correction candidates | logistics-integration, personal-health-tracker | 2+ | candidate/in-flight-extension | Keeps 69+ honest without overclaiming target closure. |
| Vertical packs | insurance, automotive, oil-gas, gxp-pharma, legal-services, hospitality, agri-food, media-entertainment, nonprofit, public-sector variants | pack-count-not-service-count | pack-overlay | No new vertical-grouping microservices. |
| Capability-tier expansions | CRM, HR, ITSM, BI, identity, security, developer, consumer, vertical benchmark rows | 244 | registry rows | Mostly §15 activation records over existing services. |

### §16.1 Honest count boundary

1. Do not claim 69+ services are all production-ready from this matrix alone.
2. Do claim the coverage plan names which services exist, which are in-flight, and which benchmark rows are capability tiers.
3. Do not create `erp`, `crm-suite`, `hr-suite`, `vertical-healthcare`, or similar bundle services.
4. Do enforce PR-143 documentation depth and the capability-tier registry before moving rows from advisory to blocker.

## §17 Implementation Sequencing - Operating Bar Before Scaffolding Drift

| Sequence | Target | Action | Validation evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S0 | Freeze doctrine | Use ADR-0316, ADR-0132, ADR-0244, ADR-0314, ADR-0315 as the decision stack. | coverage matrix references resolve; no suite language regression |
| S1 | Close ERP operating bar | For the 9 existing ERP scaffolds, complete PR-143 doc sets, Cedar fragments, ontology pins, workflow templates, and contract stubs. | governance-erp-parity-module-map passes |
| S2 | Land capability-tier registry | Create registry rows for §15 with stable IDs, service owners, and activation shapes. | governance-capability-tier-registry-shape passes |
| S3 | B2B-leader minimum 13 | Scaffold in-flight B2B services only where distinct operational concern is documented. | 56 -> 69+ target satisfied without suite folders |
| S4 | Capability depth pass | Expand existing centers of gravity rather than adding service names. | coverage rows move B/C to A only with evidence |
| S5 | Vertical pack pass | Encode industry overlays as packs and projections. | no vertical-suite service created |
| S6 | Migration journeys | For SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, Workday, NetSuite, ServiceNow, Microsoft, and Atlassian, write import/rollback journeys. | source IDs, provenance, audit evidence, and rollback fixtures present |
| S7 | CI ratchet | Make coverage, registry, Cedar, ontology, workflow, and docs lanes advisory first, then blocker after corpus remediation. | false-green blocked by direct checks |

### §17.1 Dependency rules

1. Capability-tier registry can run in parallel with ERP operating-bar work because it is metadata-shaped.
2. B2B-leader scaffolding must wait for a specific new-service justification per service.
3. Vertical pack authoring can run in parallel after base services and pack schema references are stable.
4. Migration journeys depend on stable source/destination object maps.
5. CI blocker promotion depends on advisory evidence across a representative corpus, not this document alone.

## §18 CI Lanes for Coverage Enforcement

| CI lane | Checks | Promotion rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| governance-coverage-matrix-current | Every benchmark row has tier, composition, Cedar, ontology, workflow, status, and source references. | advisory now; blocker after registry lands |
| governance-capability-tier-registry-shape | §15 rows conform to stable schema and have unique IDs. | required before blocker promotion |
| governance-no-product-fragmentation-microservices | New service proposals prove distinct operational concern and reject platform/bundle names. | blocker for new service scaffolds |
| governance-erp-parity-module-map | All SAP S/4HANA module rows map to existing scaffolds or composition. | ERP gate |
| governance-capability-tier-cedar-coverage | Every row has default-deny action/resource/context shape. | security gate |
| governance-capability-tier-ontology-projection-pin | Every row pins ontology object type revision and migration behavior. | schema gate |
| governance-capability-tier-workflow-template-coverage | Every row has activation, migration, rollback, evidence, and sunset workflow references. | workflow gate |
| governance-marketplace-deal-settlement-coverage | Commercial rows use ADR-0314 DealSet. | commerce gate |
| governance-doc-rigor | Matrix meets documentation-rigor depth and no placeholder policy. | doc gate |
| governance-doc-link-resolves | Internal and external references resolve. | link gate |
| governance-doc-graph-6hops | Readers can traverse from the matrix to ADRs, PRDs, specs, and owner services. | graph gate |
| governance-center-of-gravity-risk | High-count services get stricter review and PR-143 bar checks. | risk gate |

### §18.1 Validation checklist

1. No benchmark row lacks an owner service.
2. No D-tier row lacks an explicitly named flat microservice.
3. No vertical row creates a vertical-suite service.
4. No customer/workforce row bypasses ADR-0311 personal/work boundary.
5. No commercial row bypasses ADR-0314 DealSet.
6. No row uses connect as a generic iPaaS. remains supplementary to messenger, mail, and community account bring-your-own flows.
7. No row upgrades to Tier A without evidence.
